explanation: The left hand is reserved for personal hygiene in Saudi custom, rooted in Islamic practice, while the right hand is used for eating, passing food, and greeting. Using the left hand to eat or hand someone something is considered unhygienic and disrespectful, including when sharing food from a communal dish.
local_tip: Always eat and pass food with your right hand, even for small items like bread, and keep your left hand in your lap.

also_check.note: The left hand is reserved for toilet hygiene, so eating or passing food with it is considered unclean.
Either hand is acceptable; chopstick technique matters far more than hand preference.
There is no stigma against eating with the left hand.

sources.title: Why Left-Handed Eating Is Frowned Upon In The Middle East
